teachings.title: Acts 6: the office of deacon
teachings.summary: Acts 6 and 1 Timothy 3 establish deacons, qualified men who serve the church under the pastor, one of only two offices in the Bible, freeing pastors for prayer and the word.
teachings.text:
Now Act 6 opens with a problem for the early church at Jerusalem. The Apostles, disciples and converts, of one mind and soul, *daily in the temple, and in every house, they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ.* And to the congregation they added thousands, both Jew and Greek.

Now we know the role of the church assembly is to teach and preach the Gospel of Jesus to the unsaved, the things of God and His doctrines from scripture to the edification of the saved, and to minister to the least among them, especially widows indeed.

And even in this, the purest church with the purest doctrine, full of saved believers, full of the Holy Ghost, witness to signs and wonders by those whom had the power anointed unto them by Jesus through the Holy Ghost, people remained prone to sin, being of the flesh. They were respecters of persons. These saved Judeans favored their own in the ministering of the poor sisters of the faith, the Grecians.

Faced with this issue, the 12 gathered the disciples, those dedicated daily to the word and the work, and had from among them 7 chosen to serve the needs of maintaining the larger church and its ministry to the poor members.  This is the establishment of the biblical office of decon.

We see here in verse 3 some of the qualifications for decon; *men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom.* This is expounded upon in **1 Timothy 3:**

*8 Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;*

*9 Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.*

*10 And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.*

*11 Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.*

*12 Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.*

*13 For they that have used the office of a deacon well purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.*

The Apostles and other disciples appointing them deacons, maintain their position as pastors and evangelists, *to be continually in prayer and in the ministry of the word.*

It is important to understand that these are the only two offices given in the Bible, and that the deacons work for the church and answer to the pastor, not the other way around. We see also that this office is key in allowing the church to grow, that freed of the mundane daily tasks as the deacons serve full time to take care of matters, the numbers grew and multiplied.

In this election of deacons, we meet several key members of the early ministry, chiefly Stephen, *a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost.* We see that in addition to his duties, he maintained his soul winning, teaching and working signs among the Jews to bring them to Christ.

Stephen being so effective that certain sects of the Jews in synagogue, Hellenistic freed slaves, returned to Jerusalem from where they'd been captive, disputing with Stephen and his doctrines of Jesus Christ.

Unable to counter his preaching and pure doctrine, they instead get men to falsely accused him of blasphemy.

By getting a mob worked up by these lies, they drag Stephen before the council. We see from their railing accusation that they are twisting Jesus prophecy of the temple destruction, and misleading about the law, which continues fulfilled in Christ, and the doing away of the carnal ordinances, sacrifices and diverse washings.

We leave this short chapter in a cliff hanger, as they look upon innocent Stephen, with a face like an angel....

teachings.title: Two offices and God's plan for church planting
teachings.summary: The pastoral epistles give two church offices, bishop and deacon, and God's plan of pastor-led local churches training men and planting churches, which denominations and the Bible college system abandoned.
teachings.text:
Today we begin the series called "the Pastoral Epistles," Paul's letters to Timothy and Titus, respectively, giving them doctrine on planting churches and the only two biblical church offices; Bishop and Deacon. Bishop being the pastor, or head of a local independent NT church, and decon being an assistive role, aiding the pastor in the administration of the church.

Here Paul writes to Timothy, his "son" in Christ, whom the last Apostle had won to the Lord, and who he is asking to remain in Ephesus, planting churches.

The doctrines he teaches are instrumental in how God wishes to see our local churches established and run. In their roles as evangelist, Timothy and Titus are instrumental in passing on this instruction to those called to the offices.

Most denominations ignore this teaching, entirely. The very notion of denomination, central control, unqualified priests, unbiblical hierarchies and the like, spreading bad doctrine by decree.

Even OIFB churches, who as Baptists recognize the two offices doctrine, have abandoned the traditional training of future pastors, evangelists and church planting and embraced the unbiblical Bible College racket, siphoning off potential men of God and other young people, to feed them into a collegiate system that does more to promote and spread heresy than anything else.

God's plan for churches is to train up future leaders, be pastor-led, and to go out soul winning, evangelizing a receptive community, and eventually planting a church and sending off a pastor, who then repeats the process.

Some pastors grew so far and fast, they took pride in establishment of their Christian schools and Bible colleges, and for many, it was their eventual downfall in their service to the Lord.

teachings.title: Qualifications of bishop and deacon
teachings.summary: Churches are to be pastor-led with deacons serving, and both offices require a married man of one wife ruling his house well, sober, not greedy and not a novice.
teachings.text:
Now, having laid a baseline for general behavior that should be encouraged in the newly planted churches, to better bring about the type of men to be trusted with keeping watch over the flock, Paul moves on to describe the basic qualities required for the two offices the Bible provides us; Bishop and Deacon.

Note these aren't preists, or a honorific for high preists, the way the false denominations use the term "bishop," as we know all saints are part of the royal preisthood of believers. Rather, this is specifically about pastors, leading the flock and deacons who help him minister.

If you recall, deacon was the position created by the Apostles at the churches in Jerusalem back in Acts 6:

*Then the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them, and said, It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables. Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business. But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word. And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch: whom they set before the apostles: and when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them. And the word of God increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly;*

We see in this that the churches are to be led by those ministering the Gospel, and the day to day management left to the deacons who work for them.

Many modern churches are deacon-led, and this has caused innumerable problems, politicizing a church. They should be Christ-led, pastor in charge, deacons serving the pastor, as the Bible lays out.

And here we come to the qualifications for each office, and see they are basically the same. Married, to one wife. With orderly children and household. In all gravity, meaning he takes this first role as husband and father  seriously. Many churches have failed because their pastor, who may be a godly man, with a good wife and seemingly orderly house, allowed sin and disorder into their homes, which in turn affected the church, brining many to ruin.

Not this isn't saying he, his wife or kids must be perfect, but that the pastors and deacons be in control at home. This could mean a child act up, and being sufficiently punished, or even put out. Rather than their sins covered up and allowed due to the pastor or deacon's position. Many such cases.

Sober men. Not given to wine, but full of hospitality for others. Not greedy. Not a striker, not a brawler. Not greedy for filthy lucre, money earned by dishonest means, and selling of favor from his position. Not covetous. Not a novice, who may be filled with pride at his newfound position of power.

teachings.title: Men established in the mystery of godliness
teachings.summary: The offices are for men, never women, holding the mystery of the faith, which Paul defines as the gospel of God manifest in the flesh, with grave and faithful wives.
teachings.text:
These are *men* who are established in the faith. We have already seen in the previous chapter that these offices cannot be for women, who aren't to be suffered to teach in the church. Female pastors are not biblical, and with reason.

But of the men, they should be *Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience...And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.*

We see what that mystery of faith is, the Gospel. Some have taken the first verse out of context to bring in gnostic heresy regarding some sort of oral tradition known only to those chosen to lead, but Paul gives the answer to the mystery. Their faith in Jesus as the redeemer, giving them a good conscience.

They must also have wives who are *grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things,* because in truth and practice, though the wife isn't holding the office, they find themselves with duties and responsibilities within the church.

These ideas regarding the two biblical offices of the local independent NT churches are further developed in the remaining pastoral epistles, but sufficient groundwork has been laid here to see what churches aren't using the scriptural standard, and so, reject them. In the next chapter, we will see further, Paul writing in the Spirit tells Timothy some warning signs of false teachers to watch out for.

teachings.title: Ordain elders and stop the mouths of deceivers
teachings.summary: Titus 1 gives the qualifications for elders who hold fast sound doctrine to convince gainsayers, especially reprobate Judaizers whose fables led to the Roman Catholic Church.
teachings.text:
This epistle, written to Titus, Paul's son in the faith, who the Apostle had left in Crete to evangelize, just as he had Timothy in Ephesus.

And just as he did in his letters to Timothy, Paul lays the foundation for the office of bishop, or pastor in today's parlance, a shepherd of the flock, and deacons or elders, those who work in a church ministering, serving the flock and aiding their shepherd.

 Commanding Titus to *ordain elders in every city,* the criteria being; *blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly.* Because, as the steward of God, the man handling the affairs and overseeing His sheep, must have these qualities; *not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre; But a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate.*

Not given to wine and sober not being repetitive notions, but sober in scripture meaning not only clear-headed but serious as well. Matured in their attitudes. Not angry and wrathful and violent. Not a lover of money, corrupt, chasing after filthy lucre. A lover of hospitality and good men. *Just, holy and temperate*.

This is the model for all seeking the offices of pastor or deacon, and should be what is given as an example for all young men of the faith to strive towards. Not only those who "feel a calling," but those who in humility and meekness seek to be right with God, that they may be blameless and able to win souls to the Lord.

*Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.*

This should be the goal of all those who know Christ. Studying to be approved by God, and able to have a ready answer to those who seek truth, or who having hardened their hearts, seek to subvert it.

And why is this so important to establish, especially with elders in the churches? Paul tells us, again warning as he has repeatedly, of those reprobate concerning the faith.

*For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision: Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake.*

Even in Paul's day, even in that first century, not far removed from Jesus'resurrection and ascension, even as Apostles and disciples blessed with the gifts of the Holy Ghost spread the word, preaching to every creature throughout the world, there were *many* false prophets. Vain talkers. Especially of the circumcision. Jews who being reprobate by God sought to subvert the nascent Christian communities with deceit, just as they do today.

Paul gives an example of one such viper, who insulting the Cretians sought to keep them from the faith, and exhorts Titus to openly rebuke. To teach sound doctrines that the Cretian believers not be led astray, *giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.*

Judaizers who attacked the word of God and His churches then, never gave up, even forming their own religions based on Jewish fables, the apocryphal books and forgeries prevalent at the time. Doing it for filthy lucre's sake. For money, power, prestige. Control of others. Leaning on their own understanding, denying the power of scripture. Following after vain traditions and the commandments of men. Dead works, denying the power of the Gospel and faith unto salvation.

This is the origin of the Roman Catholic Church, and the source of her harlot daughters, subverting whole houses. Who *compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than* themselves, as Jesus said of the same Judaizers who murdered Him.

Who could do such things? What kind of man could be so contrary to all other men, that they'd seek to subvert and damn others, as they are? Just as their father, the devil seeks to? Reprobates. Conscience seared, defiled, twice-dead. Deserving death.

teachings.title: As His custom was: Jesus went to church
teachings.summary: Jesus' custom was to attend the synagogue, the local assembly of His day, even with imperfect preachers and congregations, so we should make going to church our routine.
teachings.text:
Picking up where we left off in Luke 4 yesterday, we find Jesus at the start of His earthly ministry. Having just been baptized and anointed by the Spirit, and proclaimed by the Father as His Son, and having fasted, prayed and withstanding the devil in the wilderness for 40 days, the Bible says Jesus was full of the power of the Spirit, and returned to Gis home province of Galilee, where He taught in the synagogues of God, gaining fame and renown throughout the area.

We see that Jesus ministry begins in the remnant of the Northern Kingdom of Israel, outside of Judea, but preaching to the lost sheep of Israel. In these times, synagogues were the local churches of those who worshipped God. Where they would go, not only weekly on the Sabbath but throughout the week, to hear God's word read from scriptures, to pray and to learn about God's word. The Temple in Jerusalem was for feasts and sacrifices and pilgrims, but the communities abroad had independent, fundamentalist gatherings, or churches that people attended.

**Psalms 74:8**
*They said in their hearts, Let us destroy them together: they have burned up all the synagogues of God in the land.*

Note the Bible says there was a time synagogues were of God. It wasn't until after Christ where the unrepentant Jews were made a synagogue of Satan by the Lord, rejected. Reprobate.

And Luke tells us that going to these houses of worship was Jesus's custom. It was His routine. Oh to be like Jesus and make going to church to read, hear and learn the word of God as part of our custom. To be our routine.

And of course, just as churches are today, the synagogues were likely hit or miss in regards to what they taught, how they acted, if they produced fruit meet for repentance, if they were ice cold or lukewarm or red hot for the Lord. I am sure Jesus Christ Himself sat through boring sermons, by dull preachers who were wrong on doctrine, in congregations of people who were sinners and hypocrites or holier than thous. But it was Jesus's custom. And so, to begin His work, Jesus went to church. We should too.

teachings.title: White-knuckle Christianity
teachings.summary: Christians who try to change their lives alone, without a local church and real accountability, are set up to fail and are easily misled online.
teachings.text:
"White knuckle sobriety" describes one who gives up alcohol or other addiction, but doesn't seek support, preferring to go it alone, on their own plan. Lacking guidelines, guidance and accountability it generally is a recipe for relapse. The individual is just using pure willpower to stay sober. It is like they are just hanging on, waiting for the ride to end, hence "white knuckles."

As I understand it, the difference between "white knuckle" sobriety and a "dry drunk" is subtle; both are relying on themselves to maintain sobriety, but the "dry drunk" does nothing else to change the underlying behavior or causes that feed their addiction, while the white-knuckler may take steps, as near as his own understanding allows, to make some changes in their life. Some of which may be good ideas if part of a well-supported recovery, some old wives tales or misled by bad advice found online, from friends, media, self-help books, etc..., some just plain rationalizing.

The point is that outside of proper support and absent real accountability, they are usually going to fail, often harder than they were before the futile effort.

If I have it wrong or am missing anything, forgive me. My point isn't about addiction, but the tendency to white-knuckle when someone is looking to make a positive change in their life.

For many Christians, or those who are seeking to be Christian, both believers and those believing in vain, they are living what can only be described as "white-knuckle Christianity."

They may be babes in Christ, who heard the Gospel preached and believed on the Lord, but never followed up on it by finding a church, getting into the Bible, learning how to walk in the Spirit.

They might be longtime casual Christians who once were super zealous, but as the newness wore off and the cares of the world overtook them, they backslid into old habits and even new sins.

They might be believing in a false gospel, but under the impression that they're doing right.

But regardless of their situation they will share an impulse to try to get right. To clean up their act. They might have gone through something, or having been chastised by the Lord, they're seeking to change.

But they are doing it without any guidance. Without accountability. Without a program.

They are white knuckling without a church. Without real life brethren to hold them accountable. Without guidance from older and more mature Christians that know them personally, and have an interest in their life.

And just like the white-knuckling addict, they are often setting themselves up to fail. And do, the Bible says, their later end is worse than the beginning.

The past few years have been full of turmoil and uncertainty, and the Holy Spirit has worked to convict people, leading many to try to find the truth in Christ. Amen. And in a day and age where many churches have stopped adhering to biblical principles and gone chasing after the approval of men rather than of God, It can become very difficult to find a church. Sometimes too, the person will have a bad experience with a church and it turns them off from the idea entirely, and they forsake the assembly as is the habit of some.

And sadly, many are very online, on social media continuously not having like-minded or people with shared values in their real life. And so they turn to online communities.

And like the person seeking sobriety of their own will, these people seek to live a Christianity of their own will.

They are easily taken in by people who seem to have more knowledge or experience or intelligence. People that they don't know personally. That they only know through chats or posts. And they often latch on to good sounding doctrine that tickles their ears. But having no real reference point and being outside of any kind of real support system, they are easily taken in with nonsense.

teachings.title: White-knuckle Christians carried away by strange doctrines
teachings.summary: Believers outside a local church fall into strange doctrines, purity spirals and online crusades, seeking to establish their own righteousness.
teachings.text:
They tend to be carried away by strange doctrines, weird beliefs, Old heresies dressed up as new. And unfortunately, there are way too many people out there looking to take advantage of these people for a variety of reasons. Some malignant and others just out of ignorance or because of their own emotional baggage.

And like a white knuckle addict pushing themselves through sobriety, with the nagging realization that they are going to fail hanging over them, placing the entire burden on themselves, the white knuckle Christian does the same.

They begin to either set their own standard or adopt the commandments of men. And go about seeking to establish their own righteousness. Because they're not plugged into a local church and they're not doing actual things for God, they get caught up in nonsense crusades. Purity spirals. And the other trappings of online scenes.

teachings.title: Not forsaking the assembling together
teachings.summary: Fellowship, preaching, testimony and exhortation in the congregation strengthen believers in trial and teach the doctrine from which praise and the fear of the Lord come.
teachings.text:
*Ye that fear the LORD, praise him; all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him; and fear him, all ye the seed of Israel.*

The praise and glory and fear of the Lord comes from knowledge of the doctrines of God. The understanding of His ways, the past performance of His promise, the teachings of the fathers through the inspired and preserved word of God.

Faith cometh by hearing.

In the midst of the congregation, among those that fear the Lord and sing His glory, blessing God and His holy name, we are not only given the opportunity to give testimony of what He has done for us, but hear what He has done for others. To learn doctrine and see that He has heard those who call out to Him.

We can know, as Elijah on the mountain, alone, that there are a remnant of believers.

**Romans 11:3–4**
*Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life. But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal.*

We have fellowship in our gatherings with the brethren. We have understanding from preaching and support of prayer, and the opportunity to worship God with those who have gone through what we have. To edify those going through things we have endured.

**Hebrews 10:23–25**
*Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

That communal exhortation is invaluable to a believer in tribulation. Going through a personal trial. Hearing the victory Jesus has given others provides the strength to go on.

To know the meek shall eat and be satisfied, seeking the Lord and finding Him, unto eternal life.

**John 6:35–37**
*And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst. But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not. All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.*

This is the meat we eat, and are satisfied, never to hunger again. Complete in Christ, and having eternal life.

teachings.title: Upon this rock: the confession of Christ
teachings.theme: Christ the foundation of the church
teachings.summary: The rock Christ builds His church on is the truth Peter confessed, that Jesus is the Christ the Son of God, not Peter himself, and believers are lively stones built on it.
teachings.text:
Next we see they've moved on, and having come to Philippi, Jesus is again teaching His Apostles, and begins asking "*Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?*"

The apostles say that the people say *He is John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets.* It is interesting that the popular consensus regarding Jesus was that he was first and foremost a hard preaching prophet. John the baptist, Elijah, and especially Jeremiah were known for their fire breathing preaching, condemning sin and wickedness of those around them.

Then Jesus asks, "*But whom say ye that I am*?" And Simon Peter, (*Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone*), answers, saying "*Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God."*

To which Jesus responds; "*Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven. And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.*"

Taken in context, we see that Jesus in confirming Peter's profession of faith, that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, that this truth revealed to Peter by God, and to all of us through His word and received by faith, is the rock upon which Jesus is building his church. His congregation of believers.

We see that Jesus originally calling him cephas or Peter, which translated means a stone, a chip of rock, is here paid off. A long setup punchline, used by Jesus to make a point regarding the gospel being **The Rock**, that the truth of Jesus being the long-awaited Christ is the cornerstone upon which the church is built. And we who believe, as Peter says in his Epistles, are as lively stones like him, making up the edification, the building up of the church, the congregation of which comes together on the day of the Lord.

We know that Jesus, upon his resurrection, had with him the keys to Hell and death. That rock, the truth of the Gospel, this spiritual bread, grants eternal life to those who believe. That the gospel itself is the key. That the truth of it is the rock.

And again these  things that are spiritually discerned, and twisted into perverse doctrines.

In the Catholic heresy, Peter becomes the rock, the church, an earthly institution built by men, the bread literal, and so literally flesh. The leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees added to the word, just as Christ warned.

teachings.title: Upon this rock: Christ, not Peter
teachings.theme: Christ the foundation of the church
teachings.summary: The rock the church is built on is the truth that Jesus is the Christ, not Peter as Rome claims, and taking up the cross was a literal call for the apostles.
teachings.text:
Later on, Jesus brings up the rumors of Him going around to the Twelve, who had been journeying throughout the land, now returned. He asks who do the people say I am? They say, like Herod, people wonder if He is John, or a prophet returned. But when He asks them who they think He is, *Peter answering said, The Christ of God.*

Here in Luke, the narrative moves to Jesus' admonishment to keep that quiet that His fate be allowed to play out. In **John 16**, in scripture that is taken out of context by Roman Catholics to justify their false church, Jesus replies to Peter's profession of faith that He is the Christ by saying that truth is the rock upon which His church is built. Catholic tradition twists this to make Peter that rock, and claim their earthly church was founded that day on a man, rather than Jesus and His Heavenly assembly of those who know He is Christ and believe.

It is worth mentioning only in that if their version were true, it is odd that it's overlooked everywhere else in the Gospels, and in context, not even present in John.

But affirming He is the Christ, as eleven of the Twelve believe, He again prepares them, that He must suffer and die, and rise again. Betrayed and rejected. And warns of any follow Him, to be prepared to take up their own cross daily, and follow Him unto death. That if they deny Him to save their own lives, they will lose it, but those willing to be faithful unto death will live.

We draw a spiritual doctrine from this verse, inspiration to get up every day willing to sacrifice, follow His commandments, read the Bible, pray, etc. Taking up our cross. But here, Jesus means it literally, as well. They are going to face death for His sake. They will be tempted to deny Him. To be ashamed of the word. His Gospel. And Jesus wants them to understand if they don't truly have faith in Him they will falter, seek to save themselves and in doing so, lose out on the Kingdom, He will say He never knew them when He comes into His glory. "Lord, Lord..." and all.

Again, we take from this spiritual application, and pastors will preach on how this is a lesson for us in improving our Christian walk, and it indubitably is. It is something that has comforted and edified me, and still does. It's something I try to remind myself of, especially those days you wake up not really feeling it. Cares of the world, infirmities of the flesh. Inspired by Jesus calling us to take up our cross and follow Him.

But for us it's not sleeping in, or turning to the word instead of sin or remembering to pray. For His disciples, it was literal.

teachings.title: Upon this rock I will build my church
teachings.theme: Christ the foundation of the church
teachings.summary: Posted with the building of Solomon's temple, the verses set out that the church is built on Christ, the only foundation, and that the mountain of the Lord's house shall be exalted and all nations flow to it.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 16:15-18**
*He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God. And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven. And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.*

**1 Corinthians 3:9-11**
*For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building. According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.*

**Isaiah 2:2-4**
*And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD's house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.* *And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.*

teachings.title: Baptism and the Lord's supper are pictures
teachings.summary: Baptism and the Lord's supper are the two New Testament ordinances, pictures of Christ that hold no saving power, and turning them or the sabbath into works for salvation is damnable heresy.
teachings.text:
Finishing this section, and the understanding of ordinances and their proper place in our faith, it is important to note that while the ordinances of the Old Testament were done away with in Christ, there are two new ordinances made to which we should adhere. Baptism and the common blessing and eating of bread and drink, communion, what we call the Lord's supper.

Just as the ordinances of the OT held no actual power to forgive sin or earn grace, but were a picture of the Christ to come, so too the ordinances we are told to keep are an image of Christ, a long shadow cast that we remember Him, and the faith we share as saved believers.

In baptism, the believer is immersed in water, dead, buried and risen in the manner reminiscent of Jesus. Going down into death symbolically, and rising up out of the water, born again.

The Lord's supper, likewise, where we are asked by Jesus to remember what He has done for us, the breaking of His body and the spilling of His blood that we may be saved. To recall this when we gather together in an assembly of believers to eat. Not just blessing the food in His name, but seeing the picture of His sacrifice in the breaking of bread and sharing of the wine (juice, not booze). "Do this in remembrance of Me."

This is the purpose of these ordinances, just as the numerous ordinances of the old covenant were.

But, like the Jews at the time of Jesus, the ordinance of the flesh representing the spiritual, become an idol unto themselves, and mistakenly transformed into a work of righteousness. A means of salvation. A means of obtaining grace, (which is an oxymoron).

Some heretical and judaized churches even place keeping of the sabbath as an ordinance, and a work required for salvation, despite the clear teaching that this was a picture, and done away with in the new covenant.

And just like the Pharisees, many have replaced ordinances made for man with requiring the man be made for the ordinance.

And just as the Pharisees' approach led to hypocrisy and their inability to produce fruit, men ripe for repentance, create with their false gospel proselytes twofold more the child of hell than themselves.

Damnable heresy.

teachings.title: The people justified God, being baptized
teachings.summary: Those who were baptized justified God, vindicating His word by an outward sign of faith, while the Pharisees showed their unbelief by refusing; baptism itself does not save.
teachings.text:
And when the messengers of John departed, Jesus begins to preach to the crowds about John the Baptist. Praising him, but reminding them that to be saved, in Heaven is an even greater thing than even being the greatest prophet among men that ever lived.

I get the sense that what Jesus is doing is shoring up John's reputation least any think his doubt was an indictment of the Gospel he had preached. And the crowd responds. The Bible says:

*And all the people that heard him, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.*

Now note the word choice here. Most times when we read "justified" we think of being absolved, the remission of sin and absolution from guilt and punishment by grace through faith in Christ.

But note here Luke says the people who heard Jesus, including the sinners like the publicans (who Luke uses often to contrast with the Pharisees, both men of power, secular and sinful vs who are supposed to be holy and righteous), but he writes these people who heard Jesus preach and His praise of John and his ministry JUSTIFIED GOD, being baptized in the baptism of John.

I think this is a key point we shouldn't miss.

Clearly God is not being absolved of sin here. Justified is also used in a legal sense, meaning vindication. That the evidence is sufficient to prove the argument being made. To show that they believed the report, accepted the witness, agreed with the argument, they were baptized, justifying God.

*But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.*

You see how the act of baptism by believers justifies God, while the rejection of His counsel, not believing Him, not having that faith, is evidenced by their not being baptized.

How faith is made perfect, complete, by an action that is an outward sign to man of the heart of the person, just as the refusal to act shows the abundance of the heart of those who didn't believe.

Baptism itself doesn't save. It is a manifestation of the faith, the substance of things not seen, that can be seen of men. And by not justifying God, the Pharisees show they do not believe.

teachings.title: The Lord's supper is a memorial, not a sacrament
teachings.summary: The Lord's supper continues the Passover as a yearly memorial for saved church members with unleavened bread and unfermented juice, not a sacrament, not wine and not literal flesh as Rome teaches.
teachings.text:
Now, understanding that an ordinance in the Bible is a memorial ritual, given by God to picture the thing which we are to remember for future generations, we see the Lord's supper is a continuation of Passover, which pictured Jesus, the Christ to come and the deliverance by God's promise, given in the blood of the lamb, the unleavened bread represented the haste of their salvation from sin, and literally their being cast out of Egypt following the angel of death coming for all the first born in the land.

Jesus is that lamb, who takes away the sins of the world. The bread now, represents His body. The cup poured out, His blood.

It is the same feast, the same observation. It is a memorial and a picture of Christ.

And like passover, a yearly observation, and an ordinance done only among the people. The saved. Those with the circumcision of the heart, and among the congregation. The assembly of believers. What we call today the church. A church is a local assembly, and we see in Leviticus and in Paul's letter to the Corinthians, that both ordinances, passover and the Lord's supper, were not to be done by the unworthy, the unsaved. Paul even says that God has made those who have partaken of it who aren't saved, who didn't do it in memory of Jesus, but for unworthy reasons, that they've been made weak, and sick, and some have been killed for profaning the ordinance.

And so the Lord's supper is a yearly observance, done within the congregation of believers, using the breaking of unleavened bread and the pouring out of the unfermented juice of the vine, done in memory of Jesus.

What it is not: It is not a means of obtaining grace or salvation. It is not a "sacrament," there are not ritual requirements for salvation given in the New Testament.

It is not done with wine. The idea that the yeast of fermentation would be present when all leaven is to be cast out, is absurd. Alcohol is used as a representation of sin throughout the Bible, as is the yeast in bread. Jesus did not bless alcohol and then say it represents His blood. It's profanity bordering on blasphemy to make that claim.

It is not literal. It is generally accepted by most denominations claiming to be of Christ that the ordinances of the Old Testament were symbolic of Christ and salvation, redemption and the resurrection. No one makes the claim that the lamb offered in passover prior to the crucifixion actually became Jesus. That the blood of the lamb offered upon the doorposts transfigured into His. We all recognize ordinances are symbolic, as God says, done as a memorial.

Jesus, who as God gave us this ordinance as a new memorial, says "do this in memory of me."

The blasphemous and foolish literalist view that the bread and alcohol served by these vipers magically transforms into flesh and blood (literally by "hocus pocus" said by a so called priest) is an abomination. Christianity is not a cannibal cult.

There are some protestant sects of Catholicism that don't go that far, but still make out that it is a sacrament, not an ordinance as the Bible calls it, and that while they reject the cannibal aspect, claim that their communion brings "the real presence of Jesus" to them.

Jesus told us that wherever two or three gather in His name, He is there. Those of us saved have the Holy Spirit within us and are in constant connection to God the Father through Christ His Son. The Lord is ever-present in all things, at all times. There is nothing that can hide Him or separate Him from those who believe.

It is foolishness, and making an idol of what should be a memorial. It cheapens it at best. It becomes rote. Done weekly. Done of habit. Whereas ordinances in scripture are special. Holy. Separate. Something done solemnly and with purpose.

Not every right-believing church does it exactly the same. Some do it monthly. Some every 3 months. Many do it during the Holy Week, during their Wednesday night service. Some encourage their congregation to do it in their home, with their family.

teachings.title: They which preach the gospel should live of the gospel
teachings.summary: Ministers of the word have the right to be supported by the church as Paul shows, and like Paul we serve willingly out of love for incorruptible crowns, unlike those who labour to earn salvation and remain debtors.
teachings.text:
The sudden turn in chapter 9, to address another matter of contention among the church makes me believe we are seeing Paul's point by point replies without seeing the questions he's replying to. But we can discern the meaning as we go, based on his answers. Here, some had questioned his apostolic credentials.

Paul makes the case that despite his not pressing the matter to not offend and to make the Gospel known, he was within rights to ask for a wage and support from the congregation. That other apostles, as is right, earn a wage for their service. A tithe of carnal things of meat and drink like the priests of the temple, in exchange for the spiritual things they bring to the believers. He notes that Peter and the others are paid enough to support a wife and yet he and Barnabas, being single, didn't ask for the same, even though they were within their rights to.

Those whom the Lord has ordained as ministers of the word, evangelists and pastors, preach the Gospel and so should live of the Gospel. Paul says he'd rather die than any man could accuse him of doing it for his own glory.

We know that Paul was a tentmaker by trade, and worked with Aquila and Priscilla in this during his ministry.

Paul says he is compelled to preach the Gospel, a feeling many of us have the further we get into the word, building our faith. We will see later in this epistle that some are "addicted to the ministry of the saints." Working in the church, edifying the faithful, sharing the Gospel. Would that we all have this addiction.

Paul makes the point that his sacrifice of doing without to service of the ministry is done willingly. That his reward from God would come only because he does it of his own free will and liberty. This is the same for all works we do. We are free in Christ from death and Hell. We are liberated from the law, being washed clean. Any work we do thereafter isn't by force or fear but love. It's a sacrifice to serve, and laborers are paid by the fruit of their labors, as God's law states. Even the oxen.

Those working to gain or maintain salvation are working against their will, for a price, and so the reward they get is the bondage of having to be slaves to the whole of the law. It's not sacrifice, it's selfish, and they perish for it.

Paul continues, explaining that in service to the Gospel he willingly suffers all things that it may spread, and that he may be a partaker of the glory of God.

He compares this service to an athlete, temperate in all things, training his body for a prize, a corruptible crown of laurels, while we do it for the incorruptible crowns of life given to us as reward in Heaven.

He tells us to run to win. To fight, not shadow boxing, but fully engaged. Keeping our bodies under subjection to be able to be blameless to others as we present ourselves as God's people, and spread His good news of grace. That we not be hypocritical and backslidden to those we seek to win to the Lord.

teachings.title: A pastor is worthy of his hire
teachings.summary: Like Nehemiah and Paul, a pastor may rightly be supported by tithes for his living but must not use the ministry to get rich off the flock.
teachings.text:
Nehemiah as governor over Judah, hears the cry of the people that they have been taxed so heavily during lean times that they had to turn to the rulers and the rich men, and borrow against their homes and property, and their sons and daughters. That their fellow tribesmen were changing brothers usury.

Nehemiah makes a plea to the lenders and bankmen, that God is not pleased that they have done this to their people. And those holding the loans forgive the people their debts.

*And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.*

Then Nehemiah proceeds to say that in his time, he hasn't demanded the honor or tribute of the governor's bread. Only sufficient food to feed those at his table. This is a tax on all the people, and he is entitled to it, but refused it to avoid offending God. That they did not acquire land or get rich off the position Nehemiah and his house were in. Instead he labored on the wall with them

It's similar to Paul's epistles.

**2 Thessalonians 3:8**
*Neither did we eat any man's bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you*.

**2 Corinthians 11:9**
*And when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man: for that which was lacking to me the brethren which came from Macedonia supplied*

**Acts 20:34**
*Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.*

Note Nehemiah did receive payment of food and lodging and was not left to starve. His house was supplied with the Ox and sheep and fouls.

Similarly, a pastor is entitled to some payment for their services.

**1 Timothy 5:18**
*For the scripture saith, thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.*

It's a pretty clear line between being paid for the ministry with enough to live on, and taking advantage of the position to become rich from it.

Because some have used filthy lucre to get mansions and private jets, some Christians begrudge any tithing or professional full time ministry.

But the excesses of some doesn't mean that all are guilty. Tithes and supporting a pastor are a good thing. Pastors are to not take advantage of their flock.

teachings.title: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump
teachings.summary: Following Matthew 18, Paul commands that an unrepentant fornicator be put out of the church and delivered to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, and churches that tolerate such sin let it spread through the whole body.
teachings.text:
Paul, having established the groundwork begins his reproach of the puffed-up Corinthian congregation, who have division and contention over what are foolish things, all the while, we learn, they are tolerating the worst of sins among them.

A member apparently has been fornicating with his step-mother, a sin so disgusting that even the heathens in Corinth find it gross. And by accepting this creep in the church for their gatherings, the prideful members fighting over who the minister of the Gospel they received the word from, for status and boasting, overlook how they appear to others and lose the moral authority to win souls and live Godly themselves.

A little leaven. Yeast in the Bible often is used to describe sin, and we see from Paul's analogy that as Jesus is the Passover lamb, our Christian life should be like the feast of unleavened bread that immediately follows. The feasts given by God in the Old Testament serving again as a picture of the Gospel to come.

But introduction of a little leaven will mean the entire lump of dough will be soon leavened, as the yeast grows within.

Jesus taught of church discipline in **Matthew 18**, that following a process of airing the trespasses of a brother, first alone, then with witness, then before the entire church if the person won't take the reproach, they should be cast out. And *let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.*

Here, Paul is expounding on this doctrine. Delivering one who won't repent and turn back to God from their backslidden action to Satan, cast out of the church, left to letting their sin destroy their flesh, in the hopes that either the severity of the rebuke brings them back, or hastening their death, that they be called home in grace (assuming they were saved in the first place). Destruction of flesh but saving the spirit.

Further, to keep away condemnation by the world of those who are proclaiming to be God's people, we are called to take this discipline seriously.

Far too many churches today, even doctrinally sound ones full of believers, fail at this simple task. They have among them fornicators, the covetous, extortioners and idolators...and many are just as puffed-up, holier than thou fruit inspectors, while the leaven of sin metastasizes within their own church.

teachings.title: Double honour and open rebuke of elders
teachings.summary: Elders who labour in the word deserve double honour, and accusations against them need witnesses, but those who sin, especially sexually against the young, must be publicly rebuked and put out.
teachings.text:
Shifting gears, Paul gets back to how to handle elders of the church;

*Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine. For the scripture saith, thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.*

*Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.*
*Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear.*

So elders that serve the congregation faithfully should receive double honor, double payment for their efforts. Rewarded financially for their time.

And accusations against them should be handled with respect, the same manner of which Jesus laid out, requiring witnesses and reproached privately, but publicly shamed and cast out if they don't repent.

Far too many churches only do the first half, and then often will defer to the elder and their profession of innocence. It is sadly rare that they be openly shamed and cast out for their indiscretions and sin. Especially sexual immorality. The topic can be embarrassing for all involved, and the older man's excuses taken with more veracity than the younger girls (or boys) accusations. There is often fear of the entire congregation being smeared, and excuses and rationalizations made. This is the downfall to many churches, especially those that have drifted from biblical fundamentalism, and grown lukewarm.

By not being respecters of persons in these matters, and worrying less about our own appearances, and more about doing what's right, an active lively church can avoid these pitfalls.

If your church has an elder or any member, for that matter, who engages in sinful activities, especially fornication, adultery, and taking advantage of their position against young ones, they need to be put out, and put out publicly, and police involved if necessary.

There is no excuse. Jesus will remove the candlestick of a church that does this. The hedge of protection will be gone.

teachings.title: No real presence, only remembrance
teachings.summary: There is no sacrament in the Lord's supper; believers remember Christ and give thanks whenever they eat together, and transubstantiation and real presence are neither taught nor hinted at.
teachings.text:
BTW if I wasn't clear, there is no sacramental aspect to this, no Lord's supper as it were, it's the meals we have together with other believers we're to remember Jesus, with the breaking of the bread and the drinking of the juice of the vine, or anything else that we eat together.

The idea of a real presence, or the Hocus pocus of a transubstantiation, is neither implied nor even hinted at. When two or three are gathered together in his name Jesus is there. He's always present. Our taking the time to remember him and thank God for the food, and acknowledging Christ's sacrifice for us it's just something we should do when we gather together.

People turning Christianity into a weird cannibal cult are the worst

teachings.title: The spirit of the Lord's supper, not the flesh
teachings.summary: How often a church observes the Lord's supper matters less than the spirit of it, and treating the physical bread and wine as a source of grace, as Rome and her offshoots do, is eating damnation.
teachings.text:
How various NT churches decide to engage in a Lord's supper together is really not important, so much the spirit by which it is done. Some do it in honor of the day leading to His death burial and resurrection. Some do it weekly. Some do it every meal they have at church or at home. I tend towards that, at least in the blessing and remembrance.

What isn't good doctrine is placing more in the physical eating and drinking than the spiritual application. Or placing it as a source for grace and salvation. The Catholic version of this and the Protestant spin offs have at their heart the wrong motives spiritually, and so eat and drink damnation unto themselves.

As Jesus says in **John 6**, *It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.*

Those that heard and didn't understand this were offended and many disciples left from following Christ, because they took spiritual things literally, just as the Jews condemned Him for these "dark sayings."

teachings.title: Pure religion: widows and the fatherless
teachings.summary: God commands care for widows and orphans, families must honour and support their own widows, and the church cares for widows indeed, a duty now largely handed to the state.
teachings.text:
*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world*.
...
*Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.*
...
*He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.*

There are two groups of people God has a special place for, and asks us to be protectors and caretakers of; widows and orphans.

This biblical appeal actually became a means by which many fraternal orders, Masonic lodges and other less than godly organizations worked a grift. Collecting donations for the "widows and orphans fund" became a euphemism for this kind of shakedown charity by the 20th Century. The idea itself synonymous with corruption. A punchline euphemism for illegal activities hidden under the guise of charity.

But in more recent decades, the concept, both Biblical and corrupt has all but disappeared, as the state welfare and entitlements has supplanted it. Now hardly any one, and sadly, few churches, give heed to the "pure religion" God commands us towards.

Here, in chapter 5 of first Timothy, Paul instructs the young evangelist on the proper church role and management for care of widows indeed.

Before getting to that, and continuing the thought of chapter 4 regarding Timothy's youth, and how to minimize those who look down on being told what to do by a younger man, Paul gives instruction. Don't rebuke an elder. Treat them as fathers, younger men as brothers, young girls as sisters (with a purity), and elderly women as mothers. This applies to us all, and our fellow congregants. We are family for Christ's sake, and as such have obligation for respect, and at times, honor.

Honor in the Bible has a financial aspect to it, that we give honor, payment, support, to our parents, is one of the main meanings behind the commandment. Giving honor to whom it is due is a point repeatedly made by God throughout the Bible, and this is the context of Paul's instructions here.

A widow indeed is one who, having lost her husband and not having sons or nephews (which means not only her siblings' children but grandchildren, and other younger relations), that these family members must honor her with support, that she not be a burden to the church. He warns;

*But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.*

This is similar language to those facing church discipline laid out by Jesus, that they be put out from the congregation and treated as if they are unsaved. Heathens. Infidels.

teachings.title: Who is a widow indeed
teachings.summary: A widow indeed is over sixty, desolate, trusting God and devoted to good works, while younger widows should not be supported but remarry, lest idleness bring reproach on the church.
teachings.text:
Continuing, Paul lists more qualifiers for a widow "indeed," that she be desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day. Poor, no means of support and giving her life to the faith, essentially. Further, he goes on to say she must be over 60, blameless and devoted to ministry of the church, and the wife of one man;

..*having been the wife of one man. Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints' feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.*

This makes her a true widow. A widow indeed.

Paul contrasts this with the exceptions. One who lives for pleasure rather than service is excluded, for example. And age is a factor;

*The younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry; Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith. And withal they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.*

Young women, who could still remarry, shouldn't be given the honor by the church. Even if they swear they will be devoted to the ministry, and continuing in prayer, etc, Paul says they eventually will become wonton, that is, spoiled and pampered, having financial support with little to do all day but gossip and carry on, it will corrupt them, and eventually they will seek out a man to remarry, and make them abandon their first faith, that is that God will provide for them through the church that they are swearing devotion to, and leave for a husband. Damnation in this context means condemned by others for her behavior, not losing her salvation or going to Hell.

This is all true, we witness it ourselves today, especially with welfare taking the place of charity or family support. And frequently you may see at church a godly woman, coming from divorce or a husband's death, will put herself all in to helping out to keep herself busy, and eventually get married, often to an unsaved man, or worse, a man of the church she led to adultery and divorce, and her testimony becomes an open shame. Many such cases.

We see though out 1 Timothy, and other epistles but especially here, that the testimony to the unsaved by living blamelessly so that they may reach the lost with soul winning, is a top priority.

That they *give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.*

teachings.title: Telegram isn't church: the qualifications of a pastor
teachings.summary: A pastor must meet 1 Timothy 3 and lead a real assembly, so online preachers who are brawlers and teach works salvation are not pastors.
teachings.text:
**1 Timothy 3:1-7**
*This is a true saying, if a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; (For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?) Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil. Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.*

These are the qualities and qualifications for a pastor.

The husband of one wife
Vigilant
Sober
Of good behaviour
Given to hospitality
Apt to teach
Not given to wine
No striker
Not greedy
Patient
Not a brawler
Not covetous
One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity
Not a novice
He must have a good report of them which are without

Any online "preacher," claiming to be a man of God, giving "sermons," and leading a "flock," in their "online ministry" who you have never met, do not personally know, who you cannot know if they exhibit all of these qualities, but actually demonstrates from their own actions and behavior to not hold some (say they are a brawler, always in contention, always insulting and debating, not teaching but yelling and ranting at sincere questions, lacking patience, not given to good behavior and who has a bad report because of that bad behavior, is not qualified to be a pastor.

We are making posts on social media and doing our best to study the word together and edifying one another.

This isn't church. Telegram isn't church. Discord isn't church. I am not a pastor. Unless someone leads an actual assembly of believers, in real life, they are not a pastor.

And if they are teaching the damnable heresy that you have to "try to avoid sin" to be saved, then they are a false prophet on top of it all, and let them be accursed.

teachings.title: The priest and pastor husband of one wife
teachings.summary: The holiness laws for Levitical priests mirror the qualifications of a pastor, and all believers as a holy priesthood should be separated in spirit.
teachings.text:
Chapter 21 contains more of the Levitical priesthood laws regarding the holiness of the priests, the sons of Aaron. That they may not defile themselves by touching or being around a corpse other than close kin.

That they should be the husband of one wife, just as pastors must be, and their wives must be virgins. Not a widow or divorced, or profane.

1 Timothy 3:2-12
*A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; (For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?) Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil. Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil. Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre; Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless. Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things. Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.*

While the holiness of a Levitical priest is unique, the cleanliness rituals both practical and ceremonial, and can be mirrored in the qualifications for pastor, it is important to recognize that we who are believers are part of a holy priesthood too. And for us, we should seek to be as separated spiritually as they were in the flesh.

teachings.title: Standing for the reading of the Word
teachings.summary: As all the people stood when Ezra opened the book, Baptists stand out of respect for God's word, and the called out assembly exists to read the scriptures distinctly and give the sense.
teachings.text:
*And he read therein before the street that was before the water gate from the morning until midday, before the men and the women, and those that could understand; and the ears of all the people were attentive unto the book of the law.*

Pay attention in church, when the pastor or anyone is at the pulpit, reading and expounding on the scriptures. Sit up straight. Ears open. Receiving it gladly.

*Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose...And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people; (for he was above all the people;) and when he opened it, all the people stood up*

Here is the tradition we Baptists have, of standing out of respect for God's word as the man of God preaches from the pulpit.

*...and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law: and the people stood in their place. So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.*

This is the purpose of the called out assembly. To give understanding to the people, reading from the Law of God distinctly.

*And all the people answered, Amen, Amen, with lifting up their hands: and they bowed their heads, and worshipped the Lord with their faces to the ground.*

This is the way to worship God in spirit and truth.

Notice the people were outside. They made booths of branches. It was simple and about God and His word.

The Roman Catholics would say you must have a temple to worship God. The Jews in Jerusalem had the best temple, and yet they pitched tents to hear sermons preached from an old wooden pulpit.

**Acts 7:48-49**
*Howbeit the most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands; as saith the prophet, Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool: what house will ye build me? saith the Lord: or what is the place of my rest?*

Never mind those that need worldly things, carnal, idols of wood, metal and stone. Beads. Incense. Stained glass and marble. They have to have carnal and worldly things because they do not worship God in spirit and truth. They need physical relics and iconography because they lack the Spirit.

Baptists follow the Bible.

teachings.title: Romans 16: fellow labourers in the churches
teachings.summary: Paul's greetings show saved women and men alike labour for the gospel, in local independent churches, plural, while marking those who bring false doctrines.
teachings.text:
Last chapter in the letter to the church at Rome from Paul. It's basically a post script, but there's doctrine in all scripture and definitely here as well.

Note that Paul first praises a woman, Phebe, commending her for her great work laboring for God, spreading the Gospel and being a strength to others in the faith. She is one of many women God immortalized in scripture for their labors.

Many assume because Paul reiterates God's command that women remain silent in church, and not be pastors (a position many men couldn't qualify for either), that Paul was a misogynist or something. But a saved woman is called to give the gospel and save souls and use their gifts to the edification of the church, just as a man is. That there are roles defined for us by God doesn't make us greater or lesser in His service. *There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.*

Both men and women lose sight of this in current year, and resentments and divisions surrounding this keep us from fulfilling the labors God has for us.

Paul goes on to salute and praise men and women of the faith who are his fellow laborors. Helpers. Being about the business of the Father. Winning souls and edifying the saints. We should strive to be so worthy as to be known in Heaven for the work we do for the Lord. That the *churches* of Christ salute us.

Yes, churches is plural. That's the NT Christian perspective on a church. Local, independent, Jesus-led, pastor-run, gospel-based. A fellowship of like-minded churches. Not a universal church on earth.

We are to avoid people coming in with false Gospels, extra-biblical doctrines and traditions. Verse 18 is a condensed version of the warnings given by Paul elsewhere, Peter and Jude against letting these types creep in unawares to make merchandise of the believers, and feed their bellies in the communal suppers. Taking advantage of the hospitality, and deceiving even believers with false teachings.

We are to be wise about what's good, simple or that is uninformed about the particulars of evil. Wisdom of good gives enough to discern what's evil without dwelling in it.

Paul finishes with praise of God, and in it he dispels the false doctrine of gnostic revelation regarding salvation. That while the OT saints believed in faith a mystery, we now know it is Jesus who is the Christ.

teachings.title: What makes a true church
teachings.summary: A church is measured by the word preached, sound doctrine, a qualified pastor and soul-winning fruit, not by PayPal or obeying state rules, which Romans 13 says to follow unless they contradict God.
teachings.text:
Any church that uses PayPal for donations isn't a real church.
Or that has occupancy license and obeys fire codes, ADA regs, or any other state regulation.
Or that encourages political action and particular partisan participation in secular elections.

/sarcasm

The word that's preached, not compromising that word, and the fruit of soul winning is the measure of a church and pastor. How they obey primary and secondary biblical doctrine, the pastor being qualified and producing good fruit of saved Christians, is what is important.

How they arrange their finances *could* be a secondary bit of evidence at it being false if other things - unqualified pastor, wrong on primary doctrine, adding to biblical salvation by faith alone in grace alone, mixed assembly, making merchandise of God's house, or His flock, etc - is found, but it certainly is not qualifying or disqualifying on its own.

**Romans 13:1-7**
*Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.*

*2 Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.*

*3 For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same:*

*4 For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil.*

*5 Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake.*

*6 For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God's ministers, attending continually upon this very thing.*

*7 Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour.*

If the state has rules on how tribute and custom are collected, then follow them to the edification of the Church and obedience to God's ordained powers that be.

If those rules contradict the higher power, especially the highest, God, then we defer to that higher power. Simple as.

teachings.title: I have planted, Apollos watered
teachings.summary: Believers should not form cults of personality around the ministers who led them to Christ, since one sows, another waters, and God gives the increase.
teachings.text:
We later see in Paul's scathing epistle to the Corinthians that division grew in the church there between those saved by Paul and others who came to Christ by Apollos. "For while one saith, I am of Paul; and another, I am of Apollos; are ye not carnal?
Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed, even as the Lord gave to every man?I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase."

We should not get caught up in cults of personality surrounding those ministers who bring us to saving faith, because, we are told such ministers are given of every man. All saved Christians believe because we were shown by another. Faith to faith. The who matters little. some sow seeds, some water, some reap, but all the increase is the Lord's.

teachings.title: Let your women keep silence in the churches
teachings.summary: Women are to learn in silence in church under the pastor and ask their husbands at home, though they teach their children and share the gospel, and every member serves the same goal without pride in role.
teachings.text:
Paul notes, and it appears to be an issue in Corinth, that women in the church are to remain silent, so as to no usurp the authority of their husbands, and to protect the hierarchy God created, as enumerated in Chapter 11. This is not to say women cannot prophecy at all. They are called to teach scripture to their children, to convert their unbelieving husbands with their chaste conversation. We have multiple examples of women giving the Gospel and being active in spreading the word.

But in church, under the leadership of a man of God, the pastor, who has very specific qualifications listed in the pastoral epistles, they are to learn in silence, and in their questions to turn to their authority, their husbands or fathers, first.

As Paul had previously mentioned, each member of the body is important to the goal of the whole, and the "more important" parts shouldn't be puffed up, as they have reliance on the "uncomely" parts that serve the same head.

It isn't the role but the goal.

And we each have a responsibility to that larger goal, giving God the glory and increase of His harvest. And all who serve that goal shouldn't take pride in their role but humble themselves, which is the larger theme of this letter to Corinth.

teachings.title: John the Baptist and believer's baptism
teachings.summary: John baptized believers by immersion as the answer of a good conscience, not to wash away sin, and his hard preaching told the Pharisees that descent from Abraham would not save them.
teachings.text:
The prophet who comes before Christ. The voice crying out in the wilderness. Telling all men to turn towards God, that the Messiah is coming. John the Baptist.

Jesus cousin, raised by his righteous parents, bringing people to salvation and baptising believers, by immersion, in much water.

Baptism not being the putting away of sin, but the answer of a good conscience by those who have called upon the name of the Lord for forgiveness of sin and everlasting life. The same unbroken line of faith from John to modern, NT Christians. (Note it's not John the Catholic or John the Lutheran)

He eschews comfort. Eats ze bugs. And rips face with hard preaching. Matthew 3 captures a moment of John's style of fire-breathing, hellfire and damnation preaching, in this case against the Pharisees and Sadducees. The religious leaders of Judea, come down to be seen where the actions at. Maybe to be baptized to seem holy. But John calls them out.

*O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.*

Much as Jesus would later, as detailed in Matthew 7 and 23, he calls out these hypocrites, this generation of vipers, false preachers who bear bad fruit. Not souls won, ready to accept Christ. They bring forth no fruit, thistles. False prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

Then he goes after their reliance on being special boys, born from Abraham, saying God could make a rock a son of Abraham. That their being Jews isn't going to save them. (RIP Dispensationalism).

He tells these reprobate hypocrites that Jesus who's coming, will sort them like chafe from wheat, into the fire. Cut down their tree, throw it in the fire. Brimstone-throwing preaching. Amen!

And Jesus, our Lord comes, whose shoes we aren't worthy to unlatch. And he goes down into the water, and straightway rises up out of the water with the Holy Ghost upon Him. And the blessing of the Father is given to the Son. Amen.

teachings.title: Bethel, the pillar and the house of God
teachings.theme: The house of God and the tithe
teachings.summary: Jacob's Bethel introduces the house of God, which scripture calls the church, the pillar of truth, and Jacob vowed a tithe there.
teachings.text:
Now *went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.* And there he camped for the night. Using stones as pillows, he slept and dreamed. He dreamt of a ladder, extending to Heaven, with angels of the Lord ascending and descending.

And in this vision, Jacob sees the Lord God above, and God blesses Jacob;

*I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed; And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed. And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.*

Jacob wakes up in dread and fear, thinking that this place is itself the gate to Heaven, and that the Lord must dwell here, that it was the house of God. And so, to consecrate the place, he stacks the rocks he'd slept on during the dream, into a pillar. And the pillar he anoints with oil, renaming the place Bethel, from Luz. This is the first time we see the concept of a house of God.

**1 Timothy 3:15**
*But if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.*

It's a concept that we obviously will see more of as we progress. And it reminds of this, from **Revelation 3:1**2:
